title: Self-Regulatory Organizations; NYSE Arca, Inc.; Notice of Filing of Proposed Rule Change To List and Trade Shares of the Truth Social Bitcoin and Ethereum ETF, B.T. Under NYSE Arca Rule 8.201-E (Commodity-Based Trust Shares)
summary: On 10 July 2025, the Federal Register published an SEC notice that NYSE Arca had filed a proposed rule change (File No. SR-NYSEARCA-2025-45, filed 24 June 2025) to list and trade shares of the Truth Social Bitcoin and Ethereum ETF, B.T. under NYSE Arca Rule 8.201-E, the exchange's Commodity-Based Trust Shares listing standard. The trust's sponsor is Yorkville America Digital, LLC, a Florida limited liability company; the notice describes the trust, based on a draft Form S-1 registration statement, as a passive investment vehicle seeking to reflect generally the price performance of bitcoin and ether, initially allocated between the two at approximately a three-to-one ratio by value. The notice states that this registration statement is not yet effective and that the shares will not trade on the exchange until it is. Publication opened a public comment period under Exchange Act Section 19(b)(1); the notice itself takes no position on how the SEC will ultimately act on the proposal.
why_it_matters: This is the procedural first step under Exchange Act Section 19(b)(1) before the SEC can act on any proposed crypto exchange-traded product listing: publishing the exchange's proposal and inviting public comment. The notice itself takes no position on, and does not resolve, whether the SEC will ultimately allow this particular bitcoin-and-ether product to list.

correction_note: Verifier pass: reworded the sponsor/registration-statement sentence to add the notice's own caveat that the trust's Form S-1 registration statement was still in draft and not yet effective, and that shares cannot trade until it is (the original phrasing implied a more settled document). Removed an unsupported claim in why_it_matters that the SEC must 'approve, disapprove, or open formal proceedings' after the comment period -- this could not be confirmed against the cited source text (a very long notice; the fetchable portion ran through Federal Register page 30762 and did not reach the concluding solicitation-of-comments section) -- and replaced it with a narrower statement that is fully supported. All other facts (title, file number, filing date, rule cited, sponsor, ratio, publication date) were re-verified verbatim against the cited govinfo.gov Federal Register text and are unchanged.
